inputs.rationale: A readonly IDL attribute getter takes no arguments: the #syntax IDL quotes `[SameObject] readonly attribute SubApps subApps;` with no parameter list, so there is no input contract, default, or validation rule to document.

errors.rationale: The getter declares no exception. Its exposure is conditional (`[Exposed=Window, SecureContext, IsolatedContext]` in the #syntax IDL), so outside an installed IWA the property is simply absent rather than throwing; every rejection path belongs to add()/remove()/list() and is documented on those entries.

lifecycle.rationale: A `[SameObject] readonly attribute` has no developer-managed lifecycle: the instance is created on first read and cached for the Window's lifetime (the annotation is quoted in the #syntax IDL). There are no ordering, cancellation, retry, or cleanup steps belonging to the attribute itself; the install/remove state transitions belong to add() and remove().

inputs.rationale: An interface object takes no inputs: the #syntax IDL declares `interface SubApps` with no constructor, and the parameters of its three operations are documented on the add()/remove()/list() entries.

errors.rationale: The interface declaration itself defines no exception surface: the #syntax IDL shows three operations with no `throws` clause, and every rejection path (batch rejection and per-app failure) is documented on the individual method entries.

lifecycle.rationale: The interface object has no lifecycle of its own: it is reached through the `[SameObject] window.subApps` attribute quoted in the #syntax IDL and lives as long as the Window. The sub-app state transitions the API drives are documented on the add() and remove() entries.

inputs.rationale: `list()` takes no arguments: the #syntax IDL declares `list()` with an empty parameter list and the #list table has a Returns row and a Rejection row but no Parameters row, so there is no input contract to document.

A typedef is a type alias, not a callable: `typedef USVString ManifestId;` in the #syntax IDL takes no parameters and defines no validation of its own. The derivation rule for the value it denotes is documented at #sub-app-identity-resources-and-limits.

outputs.rationale: A type alias produces no return value: it names the type other members use. The places a ManifestId value is actually produced (add()'s installedApps map, list()'s record keys) are documented on those entries.

errors.rationale: The alias itself has no error surface. An id that does not match a sub app installed under the calling parent IWA surfaces as remove()'s NotFoundError, which the #remove-manifest-ids per-app failure row documents.

lifecycle.rationale: A typedef has no lifecycle: no state, timing, or cleanup belongs to a type alias. The identity rules for the value it denotes (the manifest `id` member, falling back to `start_url` without the fragment, with `start_url` required to be unique across sub apps and the parent) are documented in the #sub-app-identity-resources-and-limits identity table.

inputs.rationale: An output-only dictionary: the #syntax IDL declares it as the fulfillment type of `add()`, so it is constructed by the user agent and never passed in by the developer. There is no author-supplied field, default, or validation rule.

A response field populated by the user agent: `record<USVString, ManifestId> installedApps;` in the #syntax IDL is never author-supplied, so it has no parameter, default, or validation contract of its own.

errors.rationale: This member records only successes; it carries no error value. Every failure path for the batch is carried by the sibling failedApps member (per-app failure row) or replaces the whole response (batch rejection row), both documented in the same #add-install-paths table.

inputs.rationale: A response field populated by the user agent: `record<USVString, DOMException> failedApps;` in the #syntax IDL is never author-supplied, so it has no parameter, default, or validation contract of its own.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The member carries only the closed set of standard DOMException names the #add-install-paths per-app failure row enumerates (ConstraintError, DataError, InvalidStateError, OperationError) keyed by the caller's own install paths, so it adds no disclosure surface beyond the API's; sub apps share the parent IWA's origin and are not a separate security principal.

inputs.rationale: An output-only dictionary: the #syntax IDL declares it as the fulfillment type of `remove()`, so it is constructed by the user agent and never passed in by the developer.
A response field populated by the user agent: `sequence<ManifestId> removedApps;` in the #syntax IDL is never author-supplied, so it has no parameter, default, or validation contract of its own.

errors.rationale: This member records only the ids that were removed; it carries no error value. Ids that could not be removed appear in the sibling failedApps record (NotFoundError, OperationError), documented in the same #remove-manifest-ids table.

inputs.rationale: A response field populated by the user agent: `record<USVString, DOMException> failedApps;` in the #syntax IDL is never author-supplied, so it has no parameter, default, or validation contract of its own.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The member carries only the closed set of standard DOMException names the #remove-manifest-ids per-app failure row enumerates (NotFoundError, OperationError) keyed by the caller's own manifest ids. NotFoundError states "no such sub app under this parent IWA", so a caller cannot probe or affect another parent's sub apps through it.

inputs.rationale: An output-only dictionary: the #syntax IDL declares it only as the value type of list()'s `record<USVString, SubAppsListResult>`, so it is constructed by the user agent and never passed in by the developer.

errors.rationale: A plain response dictionary has no error surface of its own: its single member is `required`, so a fulfilled result always carries it. The only failure paths are list()'s rejections (SecurityError, NotSupportedError, OperationError), documented in the #list Rejection row.

inputs.rationale: A response field populated by the user agent from the sub app's web manifest: `required DOMString appName;` in the #syntax IDL is never author-supplied, so it has no parameter, default, or validation contract of its own.

errors.rationale: A `required` dictionary member has no error path: the #syntax IDL guarantees every SubAppsListResult carries it. The failure modes around a sub app's manifest are add()'s DataError (manifest invalid/unparseable) and list()'s rejections, documented at #add-install-paths and #list.

lifecycle.rationale: A Permissions-Policy response header is a per-document declaration with no runtime state transitions, cancellation, or cleanup of its own. The only scope rule - the parent IWA's policy governs and a policy declared for a sub app has no effect - is stated in the #at-a-glance permission-policy row.

notes: Surface derived from the page's own #syntax IDL (WICG Sub Apps draft), the WICG explainer README, the W3C Web Application Manifest id/start_url/scope members it reuses, the ChromeStatus record, the shipping Chromium runtime_enabled_features.json5 entry (SubApps, status stable at trunk), the official subapps-demo setup README, and the Chrome Enterprise policy DEFINITION data (policy ids 1448, 1449, 1450) behind the three policies the #enterprise-policies table links. The 18-item inventory is the whole developer-facing surface the page documents: the Window attribute, the interface, its three methods, the ManifestId typedef, the three response dictionaries and their five members, the sub-apps Permissions-Policy directive, and the three enterprise prompt policies. All 8 members the page declares in its #syntax IDL (add, appName, failedApps, installedApps, list, remove, removedApps, subApps) are covered by inventory name/id tokens, so outOfScope is empty. All documentation targets are fragments of this single page: it has no child routes, and its anchors are the only addressable fragments. STATUS: implementation-sufficient. Every one of the 162 dimension cells is either documented or not-applicable with a structural reason; nothing is missing. The three enterprise policies are documented from their published definitions rather than from inference: each now carries its value grammar and schema (int-enum 1/2/3 with the published member captions; list-of-string for the two origin lists), its accepted values, the unset behaviour (default null, unset behaves as 3), its effect on add(), the precedence chain the definitions themselves state (BlockedForOrigins overrides AllowedForOrigins, which overrides DefaultSubAppsWithoutPromptsSetting - so an origin in both lists is never prompt-free), the deployment form (the definition's own example_value as managed-policy JSON), availability (supported_on chrome_os:150- only, with chrome.* under future_on and no other platform claimed), and the dynamic-refresh/per-profile features. Each policy section states what its definition does NOT specify (no behaviour for a value outside the closed enum, no origin-matching rule beyond the string, no malformed-entry behaviour, no DOMException named for a blocked add()) instead of inventing semantics. READING TAKEN, stated because it is the one judgement call in this contract and a reviewer should be able to disagree with it explicitly: those not-specified statements are an HONESTY ANNOTATION, not the documentation. Every such cell is documented by BEHAVIOUR the page states - errors by the policy-driven prompt and the documented rejection of declining it (NotAllowedError at #add-install-paths) together with what happens at values 1 and 2, context by the published supported_on/future_on availability and per-profile scope, lifecycle by the evaluation timing relative to add() and the published dynamic-refresh behaviour - and a cell whose only content were 'not specified' would be MISSING rather than documented. That is the same shape the repo's own precedent uses: v152/deprecate-and-remove-xslt/deprecation-trial marks its enterprise-policy item's errors dimension documented via a section that carries real behaviour rows AND a row recording what the sources do not define. SubAppsRemoveResponse.failedApps.examples is documented by the #examples fragment, whose remove() call now destructures failedApps and demonstrates the member with an id that is deliberately not installed, so the example shows the failure map rather than ignoring the field. CONTENT GAPS RECORDED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the page never explains the [SameObject] caching it quotes, never states whether a ManifestId stays stable when a sub app's manifest id/start_url changes or after re-installation, and carries no BCD entry (the compatibility table is explicitly interim, built from ChromeStatus and vendor signals); for the policies the definitions publish no per-platform deployment path, so none is claimed. 26 cells are not-applicable, each with a structural reason grounded in a rendered fragment (readonly attribute getters and type aliases take no arguments; output-only dictionaries and their members are never author-supplied; success-only members carry no error value; the interface and its attribute have no lifecycle of their own beyond [SameObject] caching). Structural validation cannot prove the prose correct; independent primary-source review remains required.
